newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco phosphates firm to halve debt to $1.3 bln.
newsitem.headline: Morocco phosphates firm to halve debt to $1.3 bln.

text.p: Morocco's phosphates giant, Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP), plans to reduce its debt to 11 billion dirhams ($1.3 million) by end 1996 from 22 billion dirhams in 1995, the authoritative weekly La Vie Economique said on Friday.
"The OCP debt was 22 billion dirhams in 1995. It will be reduced to around 11 billion by end 1996 then to 2.0 billion by the year 2001," said Ali Ammar, a market analyst at La vie Economique.
To meet this target, the state-owned OCP launched a restructuring programme last year, including "a capitalisation of 6.0 billion dirhams by consolidation of the rescheduled debt," Amar said.
The figures were based on an interview with the OCP's managing director, Mourad Cherif.
The debt was contracted with the London and Paris clubs, officials said.
Morocco has 75 percent of the world's phosphates reserve, but the phosphate industry, the mainstay of the economy, has been hit in recent years by recession abroad, an analyst said.
Total phosphates and derivatives exports are expected to rise slightly in value to $1.4 billion by end 1996 compared with $1.3 billion in 1995, officials said.

Raw phosphate exports dropped slightly to 9.4 million tonnes in 1995 from 9.5 million tonnes in 1994. But phosphoric acid exports rose to 1.7 million tonnes from 1.6 million tonnes in the same period, the firm said in a recent report.
OCP which employs a staff of 27,700 including 750 engineers is the world's first exporter of raw phosphates and phosphoric acid.

Morocco's main phosphates mines are located in Khouribga, and Youssoufia on the Atlantic coast and in Laayoun in the disputed Western Sahara. Its phosphate processing plants are in the Atlantic coast towns of Safi and Jorf Lasfar.

OCP subsidiary EMAPHOS and two local banks have signed an accord of 110 million dirhams to build a purified phosphoric acid plant in Jorf Lasfar, the group said on Friday. Production is expected to start in July 1997.
Societe Euro Maroc Phosphore (EMAPHOS) was set up as a joint venture 50/50 between the OCP and Belgian foam products maker Recticel earlier this year.
